permit.applies: The Guernsey employer applies for the Employment Permit through the Population Portal; a performer who isn't British or Irish then applies online to UK Visas and Immigration for a Bailiwick work visa once the decision in principle is given.
permit.first: A full-time job offer (at least 35 hours a week) from a Guernsey employer, and the Population Management Office's decision in principle on the Employment Permit before the visa.

fees.what: Short Term Employment Permit application, in policy (law firm's figure, 2024)

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Employment Permit Policy: Frequently asked questions
sources.said: Short Term Employment Permits will continue to be issued for up to 12 months, renewable upon expiry. … anyone who is not a British or Irish national needs to hold a valid immigration status. This means that any new EU/EEA/Swiss nationals now need to apply for a visa to live and work in Guernsey. … Currently the processing times for 'in-policy' Employment Permits applications are up to approximately 8 weeks from final submission (date the full administration and information is received) for a 'decision in principle'. For 'out of policy' Employment Permits applications are up to approximately 10 weeks from final submission for a 'decision in principle'. … In order for an Employment Permit to be granted a person needs to be working at least 35 hours a week (there are some exceptions), so they are unable to be granted a Permit for part-time employment.

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Guernsey visa application guidance
sources.said: All applications are made online directly to the UK Government's Visas and Immigration office (UKVI), which is a division of the UK Home Office. These applications are specifically designed for the Bailiwick and differ from applications for the rest of the UK Common Travel Area.

sources.title: Carey Olsen, A guide to Guernsey's population management regime following the new Employment Permit Policy (updated May 2024); rests on the Population Management (Employment Permit Applications) Regulations, which Carey Olsen's 2022 Guernsey immigration guide names as setting the fees (guernseylegalresources.gg answers this client with a JavaScript bot check, HTTP 403)
sources.said: There is a small fee associated with making an Employment Permit Application, ranging from £700 for a LTEP (for an in- policy application) to £120 for a STEP (in-policy application). These fees may increase from time to time.
